newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan lifts minimum foreign investment ruling.
newsitem.headline: Jordan lifts minimum foreign investment ruling.

text.p: Jordan's cabinet has removed a minimum limit on size of direct investment and stock purchases by foreigners, officials said on Sunday.
The move, which was approved in a cabinet meeting on Saturday, will mostly benefit small scale direct foreign ventures by eliminating a minimum investment level set at 100,000 dinars ($141,000).
Officials said the move should encourage smaller scale foreign investors into mostly touristic ventures such as amusement parks.
The ruling also eliminates a 1,000 dinars minimum share purchase slapped on any non-Jordanian investor who wants to enter the Amman Financial Market (AFM).
Officials said the removal of the minimum share purchase was unlikely to have a major impact as most foreign purchases are bloc sales which exceed $100,000, undertaken mainly by long-term investors.
Investment analysts are pinning hopes on further steps to ease a 50 percent foreign ownership ceiling in publicly listed firms which a top privatisation committee is studying.
Investment officials say the government is also considering expanding tax incentives for direct investment projects in non-priority sectors that now enjoy lower benefits.
